assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles turned lipid self-assembly and pH-dependent phase behaviour into the enabling delivery technology for siRNA and mRNA medicines. The physical chemistry of lipid-nucleic acid co-assembly, apparent pKa tuning and microfluidic assembly is a general principle with enormous practical impact, including the COVID-19 vaccines.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues established the early ionizable-lipid and rapid-mixing formulation concepts; Anderson and Langer developed combinatorial lipid libraries and clinical-grade materials. The group is crowded and the split between Vancouver and Boston-area contributions, plus industrial inventors, is contested; I would anchor on Cullis with one or two others.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale with multiple independent approved products, so maturity is high and recognition is timely. Part of the impact is shared with the Medicine 2023 prize on nucleoside modification, which does not remove the distinct chemistry contribution.
uncertainties: Exact allocation among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is uncertain and I have not verified patent or priority details.
Overlap with Medicine-prize territory could be viewed as recognition of the same pandemic story.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframed intracellular organization as liquid-liquid phase separation governed by multivalency, interaction strength and thermodynamics. This is a new concept of molecular organization that physical chemists recognise as soft-matter physics applied to cells, with broad consequences for neurodegeneration and cell biology.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman's P granule work is the decisive founding observation; Rosen provided the multivalent-interaction physical framework. Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded principles and could be argued for. A three-way prize is feasible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Highly cited and broadly confirmed, but the field is still debating in-cell physiological relevance, the liquid versus other material states, and the role of condensates in disease.
uncertainties: Some of the work is arguably biology rather than chemistry.
Debate about in vivo phase-separation claims and artefacts of overexpression remains unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel picture explains how a heteropolymer finds its native state, resolving Levinthal's paradox with statistical-mechanical principles. Combined with Fersht's experimental phi-value analysis, it is a classic of physical chemistry that unified theory and experiment on protein folding.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic (with Bryngelson) are the theoretical core; Fersht provided experimental mapping of transition states. Dill and Bryngelson have strong claims, so a clean three-person split is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are decades old and fully absorbed into textbooks, so it is mature and arguably overdue; the 2024 prize for protein structure prediction does not diminish it but shifts the context.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as theory deserving chemistry recognition separate from AlphaFold-related recognition is uncertain.
Credit allocation between Wolynes, Onuchic, Bryngelson and Dill is disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced a rapid rise of solar-cell efficiency by exploiting defect-tolerant, solution-processable ionic semiconductors. The impact on energy materials and the volume of follow-up science are very large.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitized cell; Park and Snaith/Seok drove the solid-state breakthroughs; Kanatzidis and Grätzel also contributed. The proposed set is plausible but any choice leaves out prominent contributors.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency gains are independently confirmed, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercialization remain open, so recognition could be premature to some members.
uncertainties: Stability and commercial viability are unproven at scale.
Attribution among six credited names is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing converted single-molecule ionic-current blockade into readout of nucleic acids and became a commercial sequencing platform. The conceptual step of reading single polymers through a protein pore is original and has had lasting analytical and biophysical impact.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton proposed the concept, Kasianowicz demonstrated single-stranded DNA translocation, Bayley engineered the pore and chemistry, and Akeson showed enzyme-controlled ratcheting. Credit is genuinely split across five contributors; I am unsure of the current status of every individual.
assessment.maturity: Technology is established and independently reproduced with large field use; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over who first conceived the approach.
May be seen as a sequencing-technology prize overlapping with other DNA sequencing candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation uses small molecules to induce proximity between a target and an E3 ligase, a new chemical modality that changes how drugs act. Understanding that thalidomide-class drugs act as molecular glues adds mechanistic depth.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced PROTACs, Ciulli supplied key structure-guided design, and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. This is a compound discovery with PROTAC and glue strands that may need separate credit.
assessment.maturity: Many compounds are in clinical trials but approvals are still limited, so clinical maturity is incomplete; the scientific concept is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Clinical validation is not yet complete.
The two strands (PROTACs, molecular glues) make a clean prize configuration uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers established a general, physically understandable way to control surface chemistry through molecular organization, and soft lithography extended it to patterning. This is a concept of spontaneous molecular organization at interfaces, close to my own field of interfacial self-assembly.
assessment.attribution: Sagiv's early silane monolayers, Nuzzo and Allara's thiol-on-gold work, and Whitesides' broad development form the credit chain. Priority questions around Sagiv complicate the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely applied for decades; recognition is arguably late rather than premature, and some members may think its time has passed.
uncertainties: Sagiv's priority claim is unresolved in this configuration.
Soft lithography may be viewed as a different contribution from SAMs.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base to another in genomic DNA without double-strand breaks, an application of nucleic-acid chemistry and directed evolution that created a new therapeutic and research tool.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and experimental development; Komor and Gaudelli were first authors on the cytosine and adenine base editors. Kondo and Nishida's independent cytidine-deaminase work adds a possible fourth contributor but I could only name up to three.
assessment.maturity: Early clinical results are promising, yet CRISPR recognition occurred in 2020 and this is a later development, so timing may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical track record is still emerging.
Possible overlap with the prime editing candidate and Liu's other work.
